key_insight: GenAI self-management advice outscored primary care physicians in six of seven rated dimensions, but not readability.
clinical_relevance: GenAI may support structured diabetes and hypertension self-management advice, though benefits for patients remain untested.
method: Source-blinded comparison using 15 standardised diabetes and hypertension vignettes.
One GenAI system and 22 primary care physicians generated advice across three simulated management stages.
Three clinicians rated seven dimensions; primary comparisons used linear mixed-effects models.
evidence_signal: GenAI’s adjusted score advantages ranged from 1.16 to 1.56 points across six dimensions (P<.001); readability showed no significant difference.
watch_item: This vignette-based evaluation assessed advice quality, not real-world safety, patient understanding, or long-term health outcomes.
paper_title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
